summary: Specifies an adaptation layer that provides a lower layer service for DDP over SCTP. It is on the standards track.

eli5.summary: An adapter that lets one fast data-placing tool work on top of a different transport.

questions: how does ddp work over sctp
subtitle: How Direct Data Placement rides on SCTP: unordered chunks, a private sequence number and a small session handshake.

tldr.problem: Direct Data Placement (DDP) needs a reliable lower layer that can carry its segments, and SCTP had no defined way to do that.
tldr.mechanism: An adaptation layer pairs two like-numbered SCTP streams into one DDP stream, sends every DDP Segment as an unordered Data Chunk tagged with its own sequence number (DDP-SSN), and uses control chunks to open and close sessions.
tldr.outcome: It is a Proposed Standard that later RFCs 6581 and 7146 update. It needs only a limited subset of SCTP, so it can run over existing SCTP stacks or be built into an optimized one.

today: RFC 5043 is a Proposed Standard that has not been obsoleted, but it has been updated by RFC 6581 and RFC 7146, so read those alongside it.

sections.title: What the Adaptation Layer Does
sections.content:
RFC 5043 describes how to adapt Direct Data Placement (DDP, defined in RFC 5041) to the Stream Control Transmission Protocol (SCTP, RFC 4960). In DDP terms, SCTP becomes a Lower Layer Protocol (LLP): the reliable transport beneath the RDMA layer.

Some implementations may build this adaptation layer into their SCTP code for maximum performance, but the behavior of SCTP itself is unaffected. To let such an implementation know that only the limited subset of SCTP is in use, the RFC uses the adaptation layer indication from RFC 5061.

The goal is a protocol that works over existing SCTP stacks while spelling out which parts of SCTP an optimized implementation really needs.
sections.eli5: Think of SCTP as a delivery truck and DDP as a shop that wants boxes put straight on the right shelf. This document is the loading plan that lets the shop use the truck.

sections.title: Streams, Segments and Sessions
sections.content:
The layer uses a pair of like-numbered SCTP streams inside one SCTP association to make one reliable DDP stream between two DDP Endpoints. A DDP stream is therefore bidirectional: the inbound and outbound SCTP streams with the same Stream Identifier are always paired.

Each DDP Segment from the DDP layer is sent as a single unordered SCTP Data Chunk. The chunk also carries a sequence number, the DDP-SSN, which records the order in which DDP submitted the segments for that stream.

A DDP Stream Session is the period from an Initiate message through the Terminate message(s). Control chunks bind DDP Endpoints to the session dynamically, and DDP Segment Chunks carry the data. DDP itself gives no ordering guarantees between different DDP streams.
sections.eli5: Two lanes, one going each way, make a two-way road. Every parcel is stamped with a number, and the parcels can arrive in any order because the numbers tell the receiver where each belongs.

sections.title: Data Formats and Chunk Types
sections.content:
An association that has negotiated the DDP Adaptation Indication carries only the Data Chunks defined here; the RFC does not require support for mixing DDP and non-DDP streams in one association, so an application wanting both with the same host needs more than one association. The indication MUST appear in the INIT or INIT-ACK, using parameter type 0xC006, and the value assigned for DDP is 0x00000001.

Two kinds of Payload Data Chunk are told apart by the Payload Protocol Identifier: DDP Segment Chunk (16) and DDP Stream Session Control (17). Both begin with the 16-bit DDP-SSN. A segment chunk then carries the DDP Segment. A control chunk has a 16-bit Function Code followed by Private Data.

The DDP-SSN MUST equal the Stream Sequence Number that SCTP would have assigned had ordered chunks been used. The SCTP SSN cannot serve, since every chunk here is unordered, and the TSN cannot serve, since the sender may reorder unordered chunks for bundling.

Private Data MUST be present (possibly with zero length) in Initiate, Accept and Reject messages, MUST NOT be present in Terminate, and MUST NOT exceed 512 bytes.
sections.eli5: Each parcel has a label saying whether it is goods or a note about the delivery. Every label also has a number, and the notes can only be a short size.

sections.title: How a DDP Stream Session Runs
sections.content:
The DDP-SSN is reset to zero at the start of each session and MUST NOT have gaps. Taken in DDP-SSN order, every session MUST match one of the legal patterns, and a chunk that fits none of them MUST cause the session to be terminated.

In the accepted pattern, the active side sends Initiate, the passive side sends Accept, and then each side may send zero or more DDP Segments with increasing DDP-SSNs. At least one side MUST end with a Terminate. In the rejected pattern, the passive side answers Initiate with Reject, and it MUST NOT do that unless the ULP directed it. This one-message-each exchange lets each end decide on resources, such as the Protection Domain, before committing them.

If too many Initiate requests are pending a ULP decision, the passive side MUST answer further ones with Terminate. A Control message MUST NOT be sent if it might arrive before an earlier one in the same session, and a Stream Identifier MUST NOT be reused while a chunk from the prior session might still be outstanding.
sections.eli5: It is like asking to join a game. One side asks, the other says yes or no, and only after a yes do the players start passing the ball.

sections.title: Streams, Fragmentation and Association Setup
sections.content:
An adaptation MUST open all its associations with the same number of inbound and outbound streams, and it should request the most streams it will need over the association's life. Because only unordered chunks are used, an idle stream costs little.

The layer MUST tell DDP the maximum segment size it supports: the largest value that avoids IP or SCTP fragmentation, or 516 bytes, whichever is larger. 516 bytes is the minimum needed for a Control message with 512 bytes of Private Data. SCTP data chunk fragmentation MUST NOT be used unless the alternative is IP fragmentation, and larger segments MUST be rejected.

All Data Chunks MUST use the Unordered option (U flag set to one). The receiver MUST NOT infer ordering from the TSN. The DDP-SSN works without special logic when fewer than 32768 messages are in flight, and if SCTP can accept more than that without assigning TSNs, the sender must refrain from sending more than 32767 chunks on a stream without acknowledgment. A receiver SHOULD sanity-check a DDP-SSN before allocating resources for it.

At startup, an endpoint inspects the peer's indication after INIT and INIT-ACK: DDP means the adaptation is in use, while no indication or any other indication means DDP procedures MUST NOT be performed on that association.
sections.eli5: The delivery boxes must be small enough to fit through the door without being cut up. Before work starts, both sides show a badge to prove they speak the same language.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
Placing data directly into memory could be a significant security risk without adequate local controls. Those threats are handled in the DDP, RDMA and security documents (RFC 5041, RFC 5040 and RFC 5042). This document adds no security risks beyond those of RFC 4960.

The IPsec requirements follow the older IPsec profile of RFC 3723, so that RDDP and iSCSI can share one profile. For RDDP over SCTP, an implementation MUST support IPsec for SCTP equivalent to what RFC 3723 requires for TCP, and SHOULD support the same level for both unless TCP is not supported.
sections.eli5: Putting things directly onto shelves needs a good lock on the shop door. The locks are described in other documents, and this one only asks that SCTP get the same locks TCP gets.

viz.caption: DDP STREAM SESSION CONTROL FUNCTION CODES

items.label: Initiate
items.desc: Active side asks for a DDP Stream Session.

items.label: Reject
items.desc: Passive side declines, at the ULP's direction.

items.label: Terminate
items.desc: Ends the session; no Private Data allowed.

messages.label: Session Terminate
messages.note: At least one side MUST send Terminate.
